text:
Maya: Heads up — I hit odd KV cache memory growth on long-context Mistral-7B runs. Paging starts and mem climbs steadily even though token emission rate is stable. Posting quick perf dump below.

Kevin: Can you paste the perf dump and env? Is this on quantized path or FP16?

Maya: Quick snapshot from the profiler (can attach full flame later):
```
perf_counters:
  kv_alloc: 32GB
  kv_used: 28.6GB
  pages_in: 423
  pages_out: 0
  evictions: 0
  frag_ratio: 0.18
  reuse_hits: 0.02
timeline:
  mem_growth: +1.2GB per 10k tokens (observed up to 200k tokens)
model:
  model_name: mistral-7b
  rope_scaling: linear
  context_window: 256k
  quant_path: q4_0
```

Li: Hmm. frag_ratio 0.18 is pretty high. Mistral's kernel layout + our slab allocator might be causing lots of tiny free holes. Also check if rope scaling or per-head packing is producing non-reusable KV keys (GQA/MQA differences).

Pranav: We saw similar with Llama-2-13B when sequences exceed 64k — allocator rounding creates many small fragments and LRU eviction can't find big contiguous runs, so paging ends up growing. Does your run show lots of small free extents?

Maya: Yes — allocator/metrics show many sub-page free segments. Reuse_hits are low despite high expected prefix reuse. Repro: run a ~120k token generation job with randomized prefixes (simulate chat with long history). Dedicated node, reserved GPU, q4 path. Paging happens to local NVMe rather than proper eviction.

Kevin: Two quick ideas: (1) Switch to a buddy-style allocator with coalescing and test largest-hole-first eviction rather than pure LRU. (2) Try pinning hot prefixes (recent N tokens) to reduce churn. Any quick A/B results?

Maya: Ran a canary build with buddy allocator + coalesce on free. Short results: frag_ratio dropped to 0.04, mem growth largely flattened over the same 120k token run. Evictions still low. However — for Qwen-like models, reuse_hits fell even further. Example: Qwen-chat variant uses non-linear rope scaling (log-interp) and our current KV key derivation doesn't canonicalize scaled positions, so entries look incompatible.

Li: That matches our model-specific hypothesis: Mistral and Llama use standard rotary/rope behavior (pos -> pos*k) so keys stable. Qwen variants (and some MQA/GQA variants) change rotary scale per layer or per head which breaks naive key reuse. We should canonicalize keys using (layer, head, pos_mod) and include a rope-normalization step when rope scaling differs.

Pranav: One caveat: the buddy allocator/coalesce introduces extra CPU work on free which regressed tail latency for very low-latency small-batch requests (<50ms p95). We mitigated by moving coalesce into a background compaction thread and keeping fast-path allocation lock-free. But this needs thorough perf/regression tests.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: kv-buddy-allocator experiment -> canary rollout to 10% Dedicated pools at 02:00 UTC. See #deploys for details. :gear:

Maya: Filed GH issue and test plan: redwood/infra#3482. Plan:
- Add unit tests for KV key canonicalization for rope variants (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
- Add long-run perf jobs (200k token) for each model variant on q4 path
- Background compaction worker + metrics (compactions/sec, coalesce_time)
- Add model-specific fallback: if rope mismatch detected, perform normalized lookup then fallback to full recompute

Kevin: Also add a synthetic that exercises MQA/GQA differences: randomize per-head scale and assert reuse_hit delta. If reuse_hits drop < threshold, flag model-specific handler.

Maya: I'll drop the full perf traces and nvprof flame in this thread and link the GH PR once ready. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
